findings.title: Pre-existing g.Update ordering nondeterminism now has two same-pass emitters
findings.description: layout can, in the same pass, both flip verboseTooShortShown (which calls printCmdline -> app.ui.Update) and have resize.observe return true (which calls repaintStored -> app.ui.Update). gocui v0.5.0's Update spawns a goroutine per call to send on the buffered userEvents channel and MainLoop does not guarantee delivery order across concurrent senders (documented directly in the gocui source: "Given that Update spawns a goroutine, the order in which the user events will be handled is not guaranteed."). This is defect class [028], already known and explicitly called out in the commit message and in task-07's Details/Edge-cases section as pre-existing, harmless debt (both writers compose the cmdline prefix through cmdlineTokens, so only which one's transient text wins is at stake, not [PAUSED] itself). This task does not introduce the race, it only adds a second occasional emitter into an already-existing pattern.
findings.impact: None security-relevant. Worst case is a cosmetic race on which transient cmdline message displays first after a resize that coincides with a verbose-hint flip; no data corruption, no crash, no availability impact.
findings.recommendation: No action required for this task. If the flakiness of the transient message ordering ever becomes user-visible, address it as a standalone fix to the cmdline write path, not by adding ordering logic here.
findings.location: top/ui.go:296-337 (Height-guard hint block and the resize-detector block, both in layout)

notes: Repaint self-trigger loop was specifically checked: resizeDetector.observe() records the new (x,y) BEFORE returning, so the layout pass that runs immediately after the queued repaint's g.Update closure fires sees an unchanged size and returns false — verified against gocui v0.5.0 source (jroimartin/gocui@v0.5.0, MainLoop/flush/handleEvent) at $GOPATH/pkg/mod: flush() is the only place gocui compares termbox.Size() against g.maxX/g.maxY, EventResize from termbox falls into handleEvent's default branch (return nil) and the SetManager-time synthetic EventResize push is unrelated to live terminal resizes. No live resize path bypasses layout(). Confirmed no infinite-repaint risk.

Queue growth checked: gocui's Update spawns a goroutine to send on the buffered (20) userEvents channel; MainLoop drains both tbEvents and userEvents every iteration via consumeevents before flush(). A rapid sequence of resizes each produces at most one repaint request per flush, and since paused mode still receives periodic discarded stat frames that themselves call repaintStored via statLoop's drain-and-discard path, the detector's own request cannot accumulate unboundedly. No deadlock or flood found; there is also no separate 'key-handler goroutine' in this gocui version — MainLoop is single-goroutine and sequential, so no concurrency hazard there either.

Ownership/concurrency checked: resizeDetector's lastX/lastY live in layout's closure and are read/written only inside the func(_ *gocui.Gui) error body, which only ever executes on the gocui MainLoop goroutine (via flush()). The only cross-goroutine read is app.config.paused.Load() (atomic.Bool), exactly as expected. frameStore access continues to go exclusively through repaintStored/repaintStoredFrame, unchanged by this diff.

Crash surface checked: the maxX == 0 || maxY == 0 guard (top/ui.go, early in layout) still executes and returns fmt.Errorf("") before resize.observe is ever called (detector call sits at top/ui.go:334, guard at top/ui.go:~148-150), so a (0,0) terminal after a pager/editor/psql return is neither recorded by the detector nor used to trigger a repaint. repaintStoredFrame (top/pause.go) returns nil unconditionally regardless of render/latch outcome, so this feature adds no new path that can escape an error out of layout() or out of the g.Update closure and tear down MainLoop.
No hardcoded secrets, credentials, or sensitive data logged anywhere in the diff; cmdline messages emitted (repaint failure text, verbose-too-short hint) carry no PII or credentials.
